title: Career Fair: Long Line Behind You
who: You (student) + Priya (recruiter at an industrial automation company)
where: University career fair booth, eight people in line behind you
what: One line of rapport, then get to it
Name, year, major, one sentence
One real detail: why this company, or one thing you have done
Ask one question, then ask what happens next

ingredients.label: Opener
ingredients.line: Hi, I know the line is long, so I will be quick. How is the day treating you?

ingredients.label: Who you are
ingredients.line: I'm Sam, a junior in mechanical engineering at State.

ingredients.label: One real detail
ingredients.line: Last summer I fixed test rigs in a materials lab. I learned I like debugging physical systems more than designing them from scratch.

ingredients.label: No wins yet, say this
ingredients.line: I read about your team before I came. I want to work on machines people rely on every day, and yours was the booth I planned my route around.

rapportSamples: Hi, I know you have a line, so I will keep this tight.
How many conversations deep are you today? You are holding up better than I would.
Is there anything you are tired of hearing today? I will skip it.

questionTemplates.label: Process
questionTemplates.prompt: What actually happens to the resumes you collect today?

questionTemplates.label: Role
questionTemplates.prompt: What do interns on your team own by the end of the summer?

questionTemplates.label: Memorable
questionTemplates.prompt: You will talk to a hundred students today. What makes one stick in your memory?

title: Internship Fair, Empty Resume
who: You (freshman, one semester in) + Marcus (engineer working the booth)
where: Spring internship fair, your resume is one page with a lot of white space
what: Skip the apology, open with interest
Say your year and what you are exploring
Offer curiosity and a free summer as the value, because they are
Ask what to build or join before next year

ingredients.label: Opener
ingredients.line: Hi, I am a freshman, so consider this a scouting trip. Do you have two minutes?

ingredients.label: Who you are
ingredients.line: I'm Dana, first year, still deciding between biology and public health.

ingredients.label: Honest value line
ingredients.line: No internships yet. What I have is a free summer and the patience to learn unglamorous things properly.

ingredients.label: The ask
ingredients.line: If you were me, what would you want on this resume by next spring?

rapportSamples: I am here to learn what teams like yours actually do, not to pitch you.
Do freshmen ever say anything useful at these? I am trying to be the exception.

questionTemplates.label: Prep
questionTemplates.prompt: What should a freshman build or join this year to be worth interviewing next year?

questionTemplates.label: Path
questionTemplates.prompt: How did you get from your first year of college to this job?

questionTemplates.label: Screening
questionTemplates.prompt: When you scan a resume with no experience on it, what makes you keep reading?

title: Company Info Session Q&A
who: You (student) + Elena (engineering manager presenting) + a room of classmates
where: Evening info session in a lecture hall, Q&A just opened
what: Ask one specific question in the room, tied to the talk
Reference what she said, not what the website says
Find the presenter afterward, not the swag table
Connect your question to your interest, then ask who to talk to next

ingredients.label: In the room
ingredients.line: You mentioned the team doubled last year. What broke first when it did?

ingredients.label: After the talk
ingredients.line: Thanks for staying around. I'm the one who asked about the rollout process.

ingredients.label: Who you are
ingredients.line: I'm Jordan, a junior in computer science. Most of what I know about production systems comes from breaking my own projects.

ingredients.label: The follow-up ask
ingredients.line: Is there someone on the platform team I could talk to for 15 minutes? I will keep it to 15.

rapportSamples: Your point about slow rollouts surprised me. Can I ask a follow-up?
Thanks for the straight answer about the on-call rotation. Most presenters dodge that.

questionTemplates.label: Culture
questionTemplates.prompt: What does this team argue about that outsiders would not expect?

questionTemplates.label: Work
questionTemplates.prompt: What does the first month look like for a new grad on your team?

questionTemplates.label: Next step
questionTemplates.prompt: Who should I talk to if I want to learn more about the platform team specifically?

title: Meet the Speaker After the Talk
who: You (senior in statistics) + Dr. Okafor (keynote speaker) + four people waiting behind you
where: Hallway outside the ballroom, right after her talk
what: Point at one specific moment in the talk
One sentence on who you are and why it landed
Ask one question she has not heard today
Ask permission to follow up, then yield to the next person

ingredients.label: Opener
ingredients.line: Your slide on messy training data got a real laugh from my row. It also stung a little.

ingredients.label: Who you are
ingredients.line: I'm Ana, a statistics senior. My thesis keeps hitting the exact labeling problem you described.

ingredients.label: Honest value line
ingredients.line: I cannot offer you much except a careful read of your paper, which I have actually done.

ingredients.label: The ask
ingredients.line: Can I email you one specific question after I reread it? One, not twelve.

rapportSamples: I will not keep you, I know there is a line. One question.
You mentioned the failed pilot in passing. That was the most useful part of the talk for me.

questionTemplates.label: Insight
questionTemplates.prompt: What question do you wish audiences asked after this talk?

questionTemplates.label: Field
questionTemplates.prompt: What is overrated in this field right now?

questionTemplates.label: Follow-up
questionTemplates.prompt: May I email you one question after I have read the full paper?

title: Alumni Coffee Chat
who: You (student) + Whitney (alum, class of 2018, product manager)
where: Coffee shop near campus, 30 minutes on her calendar
what: Thank them once, then start, do not grovel
Two sentences on where you are and what you are testing
Spend most of the time on their decisions, not their job title
End with one concrete ask you can act on this week

ingredients.label: Opener
ingredients.line: Thanks for making time. I said 30 minutes, so I will watch the clock for both of us.

ingredients.label: Who you are
ingredients.line: I'm Leah, a junior in economics, testing whether product work fits how I think.

ingredients.label: Prepared, not impressive
ingredients.line: I read your path before this and wrote three real questions. Tell me about your day is not one of them.

ingredients.label: The question
ingredients.line: What did you believe about this career at my age that turned out to be wrong?

rapportSamples: Was the jump from campus to your first job as abrupt as people say?
You switched industries twice. Was that a plan or an accident?

questionTemplates.label: Decision
questionTemplates.prompt: What made you leave your first job? The real reason, not the interview answer.

questionTemplates.label: Fit
questionTemplates.prompt: What kind of person burns out in your role?

questionTemplates.label: Ask
questionTemplates.prompt: Is there one person you think I should talk to next? I will handle the outreach.

title: Cold LinkedIn Message to an Alum
who: You (student) + Marcus Chen (alum, data analyst at a logistics company)
where: LinkedIn message, he does not know you exist
what: Name the specific connection, shared school counts
One sentence on who you are
One sentence on why him, not why his company
One small ask with an easy way to say no

ingredients.label: The connection
ingredients.line: Hi Marcus, we overlapped at State, though we never met. I found you through the alumni directory.

ingredients.label: Who you are
ingredients.line: I'm a junior in public health, leaning toward the data side of it.

ingredients.label: Why him
ingredients.line: Your post about moving from research to analytics answered a question I did not know I had. That is why I am writing to you and not a company page.

ingredients.label: The small ask
ingredients.line: Would you be open to 15 minutes in the next few weeks? If not, no problem, and thanks for reading this far.

rapportSamples: Your post about switching from research to analytics stuck with me. That is why I am writing.
I noticed you TA'd the same stats course I am in the middle of surviving.

questionTemplates.label: Path
questionTemplates.prompt: What did the first year in analytics actually look like, day to day?

questionTemplates.label: Skills
questionTemplates.prompt: What skill do people in my position usually overestimate?

questionTemplates.label: Next
questionTemplates.prompt: If the chat is useful, may I check in once a semester? I will keep it short.

title: Cold Email to a Professor About Research
who: You (sophomore) + Dr. Ramos (runs a cognition lab, gets 40 of these emails a term)
where: Email, where the subject line and first two sentences decide everything
what: Subject line: your course plus a specific interest, never Research opportunity?
Name the paper or project you actually read
State what you can offer: hours, reliability, specific skills
Ask for a meeting or a small task, not a position

ingredients.label: Subject line
ingredients.line: Cognition 301 student, question about the sleep and recall study

ingredients.label: Who you are
ingredients.line: I'm a sophomore in psychology with a B+ in your class and ten free hours a week.

ingredients.label: Honest value line
ingredients.line: I have no lab experience. I offer consistent hours, careful data entry, and the discipline to follow a protocol without improvising.

ingredients.label: The ask
ingredients.line: Is there a task in your lab that needs someone reliable rather than experienced? I would like to start there.

rapportSamples: I read your 2023 paper on sleep and recall. I understood about 60 percent of it, and I have questions about the rest.
Your lab page says you rarely take sophomores. I would like to be one of the exceptions.

questionTemplates.label: Entry
questionTemplates.prompt: What do new research assistants get wrong in their first month?

questionTemplates.label: Reading
questionTemplates.prompt: Which paper should I read before we talk, so the meeting is worth your time?

questionTemplates.label: Commitment
questionTemplates.prompt: How many hours a week makes an assistant useful rather than a burden?

title: Asking a Family Friend for an Intro
who: You (student) + Rosa (your mom's friend, hospital operations director)
where: Her kitchen after a family dinner, or a call she agreed to
what: Name what you want before she has to guess
Give her a two-sentence version she can forward
Ask for one intro, not anyone you know
Report back afterward, that is what keeps doors open

ingredients.label: Opener
ingredients.line: Can I ask you something career related? It is specific, I promise.

ingredients.label: Who you are
ingredients.line: I finish my accounting degree in May, and everyone tells me healthcare finance is its own world.

ingredients.label: The honest frame
ingredients.line: You do not have to vouch for my work. We both know you have not seen it. Vouch that I show up and write polite emails.

ingredients.label: The forwardable ask
ingredients.line: Is there one person on the finance side you could introduce me to? I will draft the note so you only have to hit forward.

rapportSamples: Mom says you hire people. I am not asking you to hire me, I promise.
Can I ask you a work question, or is tonight strictly off duty?

questionTemplates.label: Intro
questionTemplates.prompt: Who is the one person you would want me to talk to before I apply anywhere?

questionTemplates.label: Context
questionTemplates.prompt: What should I know about your industry before I embarrass either of us?

questionTemplates.label: Forward
questionTemplates.prompt: If I write three sentences about myself, would you forward them along?

title: Internship, Week One: Meet the Team
who: You (new intern) + teammates who already have full calendars
where: Office kitchen, standups, and fifteen-minute intro calls
what: Introduce yourself the same way every time, it should bore you by Friday
Ask what they are working on, then actually listen
Write names and details down within the hour
End every intro with: what should I learn first?

ingredients.label: Opener
ingredients.line: I'm the new intern, which the lanyard and the lost expression probably gave away.

ingredients.label: Who you are
ingredients.line: I'm Tay, here for the summer on the marketing team, mostly on campaign reporting.

ingredients.label: Honest value line
ingredients.line: I am useful for the things nobody has time for. If there is a task you keep postponing, I want it.

ingredients.label: The question
ingredients.line: What is one thing about how this team works that nobody remembers to tell new people?

rapportSamples: How long have you been on this team, and what were you doing before?
What are you in the middle of this week? I am trying to learn who does what.

questionTemplates.label: Work
questionTemplates.prompt: Which meeting should I sit in on to understand what this team actually does?

questionTemplates.label: People
questionTemplates.prompt: Who should I meet who is not on this team?

questionTemplates.label: Norms
questionTemplates.prompt: What do interns here usually get wrong in the first month?

title: Industry Meetup as a Career Changer
who: You (eight years teaching high school, moving into corporate learning) + strangers with name tags
where: Monthly learning-and-development meetup, mostly people who already know each other
what: Join a group of two, not a circle of five
Lead with where you are going, not a defense of where you have been
One sentence that bridges old work to new work
Leave with one name to follow up with, quality over count

ingredients.label: Opener
ingredients.line: First time at this meetup. Does everyone already know each other, or does it just look that way?

ingredients.label: The bridge
ingredients.line: I'm Dev. I taught high school chemistry for eight years, and I am moving into corporate learning design.

ingredients.label: Experience, reframed
ingredients.line: I ran 180 training sessions a year for an audience required to be there. Adult learners who chose the room sound like a luxury.

ingredients.label: The question
ingredients.line: What does hiring in this field look like right now, honestly?

rapportSamples: How did you land in learning and development? Nobody seems to start here.
Which talks or people are worth staying late for at these?

questionTemplates.label: Market
questionTemplates.prompt: What do hiring managers in this field assume about ex-teachers, right or wrong?

questionTemplates.label: Portfolio
questionTemplates.prompt: What would you want to see from someone without the standard resume for this work?

questionTemplates.label: Scene
questionTemplates.prompt: Which meetup, community, or newsletter actually matters in this field?

title: Virtual Event Breakout Room
who: You (operations analyst exploring product roles) + five strangers on mute
where: Breakout room after a product management panel, eight minutes on the clock
what: Unmute first, someone has to
One breath intro: name, work, why this panel
Ask the room a question other people can answer
Put your LinkedIn in the chat before the room closes

ingredients.label: Break the silence
ingredients.line: I will go first. Hi, everyone. Eight minutes, we might as well use them.

ingredients.label: One breath intro
ingredients.line: I'm Renee, six years in bank operations, here because I keep solving product problems without the title.

ingredients.label: Experience, reframed
ingredients.line: My whole job is finding where processes break. I hear product managers do that on purpose.

ingredients.label: Before the room closes
ingredients.line: I am putting my LinkedIn in the chat. Say hi so I know who to look for.

rapportSamples: Where is everyone joining from, and what did you think of the panel?
The panelist said the job is mostly saying no. Does that match anyone's real experience?

questionTemplates.label: Room
questionTemplates.prompt: What is everyone hoping to get out of this event? Maybe we can help each other.

questionTemplates.label: Panel
questionTemplates.prompt: Which panelist would you follow up with, and why that one?

questionTemplates.label: Connect
questionTemplates.prompt: Has anyone here made a jump like this before? What worked?

title: Following Up After Two Weeks of Silence
who: You + Sofia (hiring manager who said stay in touch, three weeks ago)
where: The email thread that went quiet after a good first conversation
what: Reply in the same thread so the context travels with you
Zero guilt, zero apologizing for existing
Add one new thing: an update, a result, something they recommended
Restate the ask smaller than last time

ingredients.label: Thread opener
ingredients.line: Following up on our conversation from the 12th. No rush, and no guilt intended in either direction.

ingredients.label: The update
ingredients.line: Since we spoke, I finished the certification I mentioned and used it on a first real project.

ingredients.label: Proof you listened
ingredients.line: I also read the case study you recommended. You were right about the third chapter.

ingredients.label: The smaller ask
ingredients.line: Is 15 minutes still realistic this month? If the timing is wrong, tell me when to try again and I will.

rapportSamples: Hiring timelines slip, I get it. This is a nudge, not a complaint.
If the answer is not now, that is a useful answer too.

questionTemplates.label: Status
questionTemplates.prompt: Has anything changed about the role or the timeline since we spoke?

questionTemplates.label: Redirect
questionTemplates.prompt: If this role is frozen, is there someone else I should be talking to?

questionTemplates.label: Close
questionTemplates.prompt: Should I check back in a month, or close the loop here?
